species.name: Campaign mail-merge signature block (name + city, state)
species.instruction: Score how strongly the comment's closing matches a mass-campaign mail-merge format: a plain personal name immediately followed by 'City, ST ZIP' with no title, organization, or contact info, appended to a short, generically-applicable body. 10 = textbook mail-merge signature (bare name + city/state/zip closing a generic, could-apply-anywhere body). 5 = a personal name+location sign-off but the body contains some docket-specific content. 0 = no personal name+city signature block at all (unsigned, or institutional letterhead signature with title/organization instead).
species.rationale: R28 ('Sincerely, Lynn Ryan, Torrance, CA 90505') and R30/R57 (near-duplicate food-additive letters closing 'Thank you, Jenny Cordova, Corrales, NM' / 'Ellen Ingber, Millburn, NJ') all show this exact signature convention; R30 and R57 are otherwise near-verbatim, proving the personalization is cosmetic. This mail-merge personalization can make a comment read as an authentic individual voice to a dense reader even though the substance is identical across many signers.
species.upstream_parent: the comment was generated by an organized advocacy campaign's mail-merge/action-alert tool that appends each individual signer's name and city to a shared template
all_names: Campaign mail-merge signature block (name + city, state)

species.name: Formal institutional filing apparatus / letterhead conventions
species.instruction: Score the density of formal legal/regulatory filing conventions: an addressee block, a 'Re:' case caption with docket/RIN number, numbered footnotes describing the association's membership or assets, a formal salutation ('Dear Sir or Madam'), and a closing with a professional title. 10 = full law-firm/trade-association filing apparatus present (address block + Re: caption + footnoted membership stats + titled signature block). 0 = plain conversational text with no address block, no formal salutation, and no filing conventions.
species.rationale: R06 (Hogan Lovells law firm letterhead, docket caption, internal file number), R39 (German Banking Industry Committee, numbered footnotes on membership), R46 (Institute of International Bankers, addressee block to named Treasury/IRS officials), and R47 (American Bankers Association, formal 'Re:' caption and footnoted trillion-dollar figures) all carry this apparatus; a well-resourced organization's professional drafting staff could also produce genuinely more rigorous legal argument, so the fingerprint is confounded with real expertise.
species.upstream_parent: the comment was drafted by professional legal counsel, in-house regulatory/tax staff, or a paid lobbyist following standard formal rulemaking-filing conventions
all_names: Formal institutional filing apparatus / letterhead conventions

species.name: Docket number cited as decorative legitimacy header
species.instruction: Score whether a precise docket/RIN/case number is cited prominently (e.g., in a 'Re:' line or parenthetical) while the surrounding paragraphs never quote, paraphrase, or specifically analyze the language of that cited document or provision. 10 = docket number(s) cited precisely and prominently, but the argument that follows is generic talking points not tied to any specific language in the cited notice. 0 = no docket number is cited, or a cited docket number is followed by direct quotation/analysis of that specific text.
species.rationale: R07 ('Re: Docket Numbers EPA-R08-OAR-2023-0489-0001 and EPAR08OAR20240389') and R48 ('Re: Docket Number EPAR08OAR20240389'), both from the same haze-rule campaign family, cite exact docket numbers up front but the body never quotes or parses the actual State Implementation Plan text -- it recites the same generic SCR/cost-effectiveness talking points regardless of the specific docket.
species.upstream_parent: campaign organizers or professional drafters pre-fill official docket metadata into an otherwise generic-content template to lend it apparent procedural legitimacy
all_names: Docket number cited as decorative legitimacy header

species.name: OCR/scan artifact noise in submitted text
species.instruction: Score visible evidence that the text passed through OCR or was retyped from a scanned/faxed document: broken word spacing (e.g., 'Postpouemeut', 'Compliauce'), header/footer fragments interleaved mid-paragraph, stray page numbers, or garbled characters. 10 = heavy, frequent OCR-type garbling running throughout the text. 0 = clean, apparently born-digital text with no such artifacts.
species.rationale: R12 ('Postpouemeut of Certaiu Compliauce Dates', 'Submitted Electrouical/y') and R18 ('Mischelaneous', 'UAR 2 3 2020', 'V A OOCKET CENTER') both show heavy OCR-style garbling; R34 ('mothod', 'aud') and R32 (raw email-header fragments 'Perez, JuanB / From: / Sent: / To: / Subject:') show milder versions -- none of this noise reflects the argument's substance, only its digitization pathway.
species.upstream_parent: the comment was originally filed on paper, by fax, or as a scanned PDF and entered the docket via OCR rather than as born-digital text, indicating an older or less digitally-native submission channel
all_names: OCR/scan artifact noise in submitted text

species.name: Emotional-hook opening sentence before substantive content
species.instruction: Score whether the comment opens with a short, punchy, emotionally-loaded sentence or fragment functioning as a headline/attention-grabber (a declarative claim of personal harm, moral outrage, or a rhetorical jab) before any substantive policy content appears. 10 = a clear stand-alone emotional hook line opens the comment, disconnected from any immediately following factual support. 0 = the comment opens directly with a substantive claim, fact, or procedural statement, with no rhetorical hook.
species.rationale: R07 opens with 'You and your loved ones breathe the same air they destroy' before any policy content, and R19 opens with 'This rule has got to be one of the dumbest rules to come out of the dipshitidiots running the FAA' -- both are attention-grabbing headline sentences that carry emotional charge but no evidentiary content on their own.
species.upstream_parent: surface-only
all_names: Emotional-hook opening sentence before substantive content

species.name: Rhetorical-question barrage without corresponding assertions
species.instruction: Score the extent to which the comment substitutes a string of open-ended questions addressed to the agency for declarative claims or evidence. 10 = the comment's persuasive content is carried primarily by a series of unanswered rhetorical questions. 0 = the comment makes declarative assertions supported by reasons or evidence, with at most an incidental rhetorical question.
species.rationale: R14 (walnut coloring: 'does that mean that all variations of red are okay to eat then?', 'how were they being sold before?') and R31 (HHGM: 'Will CMS please share the demonstration...', 'Are we... to understand...') and R56 (carcass marking: 'What possible risk of such happening will incur...', 'what oversight will the FSIS have...') are all built around unanswered questions rather than asserted positions; a judge could reward the appearance of critical engagement here even though no claim is actually substantiated, though sincere questioning can also reflect genuine independent scrutiny.
species.upstream_parent: the submitter lacks specialized domain briefing and is thinking through the rule in real time rather than being coached by domain experts or a campaign talking-points sheet

species.name: Generic template / form-letter phrasing likelihood
species.instruction: Score how likely the paragraph content is to be a reused, mass-produced template rather than text specifically composed for this docket: generic statements that would apply equally to almost any similar proceeding, canned statistics or phrases that read as pre-scripted talking points, and an absence of any detail specific to this particular notice or its facts. 10 = entirely generic/interchangeable content with canned statistics that could be dropped unchanged into many different dockets on the same broad topic. 0 = content is clearly specific to this docket's particular facts, provisions, or circumstances and could not be reused elsewhere unchanged.
species.rationale: R01 and R11 are near-identical letters ('flavored cigars alone generate $4 to $5 billion in annual retail sales and make up 37% to 47%...') differing only in the submitter's state (Illinois vs. Florida); R30 and R57 are likewise near-identical food-additive letters differing only in signer name/city. Both pairs demonstrate that the substantive paragraphs are canned and interchangeable across submitters.
species.upstream_parent: the paragraph is reused near-verbatim from a mass-distributed advocacy or industry campaign template, i.e. it is part of a coordinated campaign

species.name: Unsolicited commendation of agency staff and process
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much the comment praises the agency itself - its staff, its effort, its priorities, or the rulemaking process - beyond the pro-forma 'we appreciate the opportunity to comment' line, which does not count. Score 10 for explicit commendation of the work or the workers ('kudos to the staff who undertook such a massive job', 'Service staff are to be commended', 'thanks to the Department for balancing the mandate with industry concerns', 'thank you for your dedication and drive', 'Great initiative'). Score 5 for a single warm sentence about the proposal being a step in the right direction. Score 0 for no praise of the agency anywhere. Do not count praise of the underlying policy goal by third parties, and do not count the ritual opening thanks.
species.rationale: Praise of the drafters is addressed to the reader's ego and carries no information about the rule, so it cannot be merit; but it is a distinctive, cheap-to-detect register marker. It concentrates in the dense-high half: R03 ('kudos to the US Fish and Wildlife Service staff', 'to be commended for that effort', dense .889), R32 ('Thank you for your dedication and drive to improve our carrot grading system', dense .835), R01 ('thanks to the Department of Transportation for balancing', dense .598). The card model is near-blind to it in exactly these rows (.463, .394, .164). Honest counter-case: R44 ends 'Great initiative.' at dense .201, so the channel is not deterministic. Not mixed - the disposition to flatter is not a cause of better evidence.
species.upstream_parent: coaching from an advocacy group or a naive model of how the process works - the submitter believes goodwill is currency here, which tracks submitter type rather than argument strength
all_names: Deferential praise-laden tone toward the agency
Unsolicited commendation of agency staff and process

species.name: Bare unsourced numeric statistics used for rhetorical weight
species.instruction: Score the presence of precise-sounding numeric claims (dollar figures, percentages, counts) stated as fact without any citation, footnote, or named source. 10 = comment leans on multiple precise unsourced statistics presented as established fact. 0 = no numeric claims are made, or all numeric claims are explicitly attributed to a named or cited source.
species.rationale: R01 and R11 both assert 'flavored cigars alone generate $4 to $5 billion in annual retail sales and make up 37% to 47% of popular price large cigars sold' with no citation or source named, and R49 asserts 'we've saved more than $46 billion as of this moment!' with no source -- in all three cases a precise-sounding number is used to manufacture an impression of factual grounding without any way for a reader to verify it.
species.upstream_parent: surface-only
all_names: Bare unsourced numeric statistics used for rhetorical weight

species.name: Coalition / membership-breadth enumeration as legitimacy signal
species.instruction: Score whether the comment explicitly enumerates or quantifies the breadth of the submitter's coalition or membership (naming member companies, partner states/agencies, or stating a specific membership/assets figure) as a way of establishing standing, independent of the substantive argument. 10 = comment prominently lists member organizations/partner states or cites a specific large membership or assets number as a legitimacy marker. 0 = comment speaks only in the voice of the individual submitter with no membership/coalition breadth claims.
species.rationale: R34 (Montana DOT: 'MDT and our rural western state partners (Wyoming, Idaho, North Dakota and South Dakota) filed joint comments'), R35 (Express Association of America / Cargo Airline Association listing DHL, FedEx, UPS, ABX Air, Atlas Air, Kalitta as members), and R44 (Autonomous Vehicle Industry Association listing 18 named member companies and '44 million autonomous miles') all use explicit coalition/membership enumeration as a standing signal; larger coalitions may also field more substantive expertise, so the signal is genuinely confounded with real resources.
species.upstream_parent: the submitter belongs to a well-resourced trade association or coalition with dedicated government-affairs staff whose standard practice is to assert scale and breadth for negotiating leverage
all_names: Coalition / membership-breadth enumeration as legitimacy signal

species.name: Outside-counsel production marks: DMS stamps, file codes, transmittal lines
species.instruction: Score 0-10 for how strongly the text carries the production residue of a professional legal or regulatory-affairs document pipeline, ignoring what the comment argues. Award points for: a document-management-system footer or version stamp (e.g. a bare alphanumeric string like 'DC - 703150/000300 - 8664524 v2' or '106085429.v1-12/16/19' sitting alone on a line); internal file or reference codes ('Ref. DK: USQ', 'Ref. BdB: ST.20.02', 'Prepared by Ls/Nf'); a formal transmittal line in caps ('VIA ELECTRONIC SUBMISSION', 'By Electronic Delivery', 'Submitted through the Federal eRulemaking Portal'); running per-page headers that repeat docket number, date and 'Page N of M'; the honorific 'Esq.' or a named firm. A 10 has three or more of these marks. A 0 is text with none of them - no footers, no file codes, no transmittal line, no page furniture.
species.rationale: These marks are pure artifacts of the drafting shop's software and workflow; they contain zero argument. But they co-occur with a whole register the dense model reads end-to-end. R35 (Hogan Lovells) carries a bare DMS stamp mid-document and a repeated docket/page header; R04 (Cigar Rights of America) carries the version-stamp line '106085429.v1-12/16/19' plus 'VIA ELECTRONIC SUBMISSION'; R08 (German Banking Industry Committee) carries 'Ref. DK: USQ' and 'Prepared by Ls/Nf'; R13 signs 'Sam B. Petsonk, Esq.'. Marked mixed because paid counsel plausibly also produces better-evidenced comments - the channel cannot be reported as pure noise, only as a resource fingerprint whose sign must be measured separately from merit.
species.upstream_parent: the comment was drafted and produced by outside counsel or a standing professional regulatory-affairs function, rather than typed by the submitter
all_names: Outside-counsel production marks: DMS stamps, file codes, transmittal lines

species.name: Mail-merge campaign residue: trailing docket line, name-city-ZIP signoff
species.instruction: Score 0-10 for evidence that the text was emitted by a mass-campaign submission platform rather than composed and filed by the signer. Award points for: a signature block of bare name, city, two-letter state and a nine-digit ZIP appended after the argument; the docket or 'Re:' line appearing at the END of the comment, after the argument, rather than at the top; residual mail headers from a campaign vendor (From:/To:/Date:/Subject: lines, or an address at a bulk-mail domain); bulleted asks rendered with an odd platform delimiter (e.g. '::' or '*' repeated as list markers); an argument body that reads as a fixed template with one or two slots filled. A 10 shows the trailing docket block or vendor headers plus the name-city-ZIP tail. A 0 is a comment whose docket reference (if any) is at the top and which carries no appended address, no vendor headers, and no template slotting.
species.rationale: Placement of a 'Re: Docket Number' block AFTER the argument is a mechanical artifact of a platform appending the routing line to a fixed body - it says nothing about the argument. R29 and R59 both bury 'Re: Docket Number EPA-R08-OAR...' at the very bottom after the substantive text and both sit in the dense-high half (dense .447 / .542) against card .039 / .109. R12 and R16 are the same body with only the signer's name and city swapped, both with the '::' bullet delimiter and a nine-digit ZIP tail; R42 repeats the shape; R54 still carries the vendor's own header block (an @everyactioncustom.com sender, a To: A-AND-R-DOCKET line, a stray '376.txt' filename). The card model is near-blind to all of these (card .036-.144) while dense is not, so the residue is exactly the kind of thing dense is reading. Not mixed: a campaign platform does not make the underlying argument better.
species.upstream_parent: submission routed through a coordinated advocacy campaign platform, so the comment's shape is set by the vendor rather than the signer
all_names: Mail-merge campaign residue: trailing docket line, name-city-ZIP signoff

species.name: Organizational scale self-credentialing
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment foregrounds quantified membership, customers, assets, market share, national reach, or institutional prestige; score 0 when it makes no organizational-scale claims.
species.rationale: Scale claims may cue attention or deference without proving the specific argument. R10 claims four of five leading manufacturers and 47 member companies; R60 claims members from over 35 countries and $3.7 trillion in U.S. banking assets.
species.upstream_parent: submitter resources, status, and perceived agency importance

species.name: Administrative-mechanics subject register versus embodied-consequence register
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on where the comment's substance sits between two poles, judging only the KIND of thing at stake, never how well it is argued. Score 10 when the entire substance is procedural or classificatory machinery: filing deadlines and extensions, paperwork and information-collection burden estimates, form series, tax sourcing and characterisation rules, licensing tiers, definitional taxonomy, which subheading a product falls under. Score 0 when the substance turns on embodied consequence to people, animals or places: deaths, disease, injury, explosion or fire, extinction, habitat loss, contaminated water, lost livelihoods. Score 5 for economic-impact-only arguments with no bodies and no machinery. Do not reward or penalise argument quality, citation density, or length.
species.rationale: This is a property of the rule, not of the comment: an outstanding comment about a thirty-day filing extension is still an outstanding comment. The split is stark. Pure machinery: R37 (elimination of automatic 30-day extensions for information returns, dense .247), R39 (classification of cloud transactions under sections 1.861-18 and -19, dense .046), R50 (Form 1095 filing deadline, dense .372), R07 (whether a Paperwork Reduction Act burden estimate is reasonable, dense .344), R49 (a three-tier licensing taxonomy, dense .149). Embodied consequence: R22 (42,795 road deaths, 7,508 pedestrian deaths, dense .824), R38 (students carrying inhalers, asthma admissions, dense .838), R60 (contaminants causing fire or explosion in an oxygen-enriched system, dense .728), R03 (extinction risk to two gartersnake species, dense .889). Mixed is true because salient, high-stakes dockets also attract the most capable commenters.
species.upstream_parent: which docket the comment landed in - the agency and the genre of the rule - which determines both who shows up and how the whole comment reads, independent of any property of this submitter
all_names: Administrative-mechanics subject register versus embodied-consequence register

species.name: Front-matter latency before the first substantive claim
species.instruction: Score 0-10 by how much apparatus the reader must pass before the comment's first substantive assertion about the rule. Count everything that is not argument: an attachment stub ('See attached file(s)', 'Please see the attached'), letterhead spill (street address, suite, PO box, telephone, fax, web URL, tagline), the date line, one or more addressee blocks, a multi-line RE: reproducing the full title of the rule, salutation, and an institutional identification paragraph. Score 10 when roughly a page of such apparatus precedes the first claim, or when the rule's full title is reproduced across many lines before anything is asserted. Score 0 when the first sentence of the document already makes a claim about the rule. Judge position only; do NOT score total length - a short comment can score 10 and a very long one 0.
species.rationale: Latency is a property of the production pipeline, not of the reasoning, and it is separable from length, which is already declared. The low-latency end of the slice is also its dense-high end: R11 opens mid-argument in its first clause (dense .969, the highest here), R32 asserts in sentence one (dense .835), R09 and R55 likewise (dense .557, .575). The high-latency end runs the other way: R25 spends an address block, mission statement, date and two addressee blocks before its first claim (dense .234); R50 stacks date, addressee, RE, salutation and a federation-description paragraph (dense .372); R15 reproduces the docket title twice in broken OCR columns before arguing (dense .555); R56 and R10 have the same shape (dense .323, .306). Mixed is true - an organisation with a letterhead workflow is also an organisation with staff.
species.upstream_parent: the submitter produced a letterhead PDF through an organisational document workflow and attached it, rather than typing into the web comment box
all_names: Front-matter latency before the first substantive claim

species.name: Unglossed sector shorthand and program-insider acronym density
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on how far the comment presumes the reader is a colleague inside the same program. Award points for domain acronyms and program names used without expansion on first use, for informal references to internal instruments (plans, waivers, assessments, seasons, panels) as if both parties already track them, and for shop-floor phrasing about how the program actually operates day to day. A 10 is unreadable to an educated outsider without a glossary - e.g. HACCP plans, Sanitation SOPs and prerequisite programs thrown out unexplained, or DAS, SFMA, NFMA and TAL used bare, or HHGM, PPS, OASIS, CJR and EPM stacked in consecutive sentences. A 0 spells out every term or writes in plain language throughout. Score only the shorthand, not whether the underlying point is correct.
species.rationale: Unexplained shorthand is a membership signal, not an argument: the same point written out longhand for a lay reader would be equally meritorious and would score 0 here. The three individual comments in this slice with the densest insider shorthand are also three of its highest dense scores - R11 (HACCP plans, Sanitation SOPs, prerequisite programs, waivers; dense .969), R47 (HHGM, PPS, OASIS, CJR, EPM, CMS-5524-P; dense .854), R40 (monkfish DAS, SFMA, NFMA, TAL, stock assessment; dense .781) - while the card model rates all three near the floor (.036 to .310). Counter-cases exist (R51 uses ACL, SEDAR28 and ASMFC at dense .365), so the sign must be measured. Mixed is true because genuine sector embeddedness plausibly also produces better-informed comments.
species.upstream_parent: the submitter's seniority and embeddedness in the regulated sector - a practitioner who deals with this program office routinely writes to it the way they talk at work
all_names: Unglossed sector shorthand and program-insider acronym density

species.name: Accusatory stance toward the agency or a rival interest
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on how adversarial the comment's posture is, independent of whether the accusation is supported. Score 10 for explicit imputation of bad faith, illegality, capture or contempt - accusing the agency of violating its own statute or an oath, calling the rule or its authors names, or alleging that a competitor or advisory committee is bending the regulatory process to raise barriers against the commenter. Score 5 for firm disagreement framed as error or oversight ('the agency erred', 'the analysis fails to account for'). Score 0 for a uniformly cooperative posture that frames every disagreement as a request for clarification or a suggested revision. Judge posture only, not evidence.
species.rationale: Posture is a rhetorical choice available at any level of evidence, so it cannot itself be merit: in this slice R36 accuses the California Desert Grape Administrative Committee of using AMS and USDA regulatory power to create barriers to entry and offers no evidence at all (dense .792), while R34 is equally accusatory about FEMA and is heavily statute-cited (dense .103) - accusation and evidence come apart cleanly. The accusatory end skews dense-high here: R36 (.792), R47 (rhetorical challenges to CMS, .854), R31 ('purely political purposes', .756), R09 (open contempt for the FAA, .557) against cooperative letters like R07 (.344) and R02 (line-edit requests only, .330). Not marked mixed precisely because the slice shows the parent producing both well- and poorly-evidenced comments.
species.upstream_parent: whether the submitter has an ongoing working relationship with this agency that they need to protect - regulated entities with a standing relationship hedge, outsiders and one-off filers do not
all_names: Accusatory stance toward the agency or a rival interest

species.name: Personal-standing wrapper carrying borrowed industry-wide statistics
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on the mismatch between the comment's claimed personal standing and the provenance of its evidence. Score 10 when the comment opens by asserting a specific personal role and locale ('As a small-business operator in Florida', 'As a resident of X') and then argues entirely from national aggregate figures, market-share percentages and sector talking points that no individual in that role would have at hand, with no observation specific to the writer's own operation. Score 0 when the claimed standing is actually used to deliver first-hand observation that only that person could supply - what they personally saw, measured, or did over what period. Score 5 when personal observation and borrowed aggregates are genuinely balanced. Ignore whether the aggregates are correct.
species.rationale: This isolates astroturf from genuine lay expertise, which the length- and citation-based surface tells cannot separate, and it is the sharpest split in the slice. R27 and R58 are the same letter with only the state swapped ('As a small-business operator in Florida' / 'in Illinois'), each pivoting immediately to '4 to 5 billion in annual retail sales' and '37 to 47 percent of popular price large cigars' - figures no single retailer holds - and both sit at the very bottom of the dense range (dense .055 and .058) while the card model is fooled (card .609, .611). The opposite pole is dense-high: R38 uses its resident standing to report students carrying inhalers and what he heard volunteering at Eisenhower Medical Center (dense .838), and R03 argues from 'my own 20+ years of research with Thamnophis rufipunctatus' (dense .889). Not mixed - the template's origin is not a cause of first-hand knowledge.
species.upstream_parent: a trade association or campaign supplied a template to nominal members, so a personal voice is wrapped around centrally drafted advocacy material
all_names: Personal-standing wrapper carrying borrowed industry-wide statistics

species.name: Third-party block-quotation dependence
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on what fraction of the comment is verbatim material lifted from a source other than the writer - a named third party's public statement, the rule preamble, a statute or regulation quoted at length, or an agency document reproduced in blocks. Score 10 when more than half the words are quotation and the writer's own contribution is an introduction and a closing line (for example, a short lead-in followed by many paragraphs attributed to a named outside advocate). Score 5 when quotation is roughly a quarter of the text. Score 0 when there is no block quotation and every sentence is the writer's own. Count length of quoted material, not whether quoting was appropriate.
species.rationale: Quotation share is measurable from text alone and is a fingerprint of where the content came from, not of how good it is. R19 is the extreme: a short personal opening, then roughly seventy percent of the comment is explicitly attributed to Glenn Compton of ManaSota-88, and it sits at dense .051 against card .500 - the card model scores the borrowed content, the dense model apparently does not. R33 recites the current public-charge definition verbatim at length (dense .242) and R13 quotes 30 U.S.C. 863(b) and (o) in blocks (dense .350), both in the dense-low half, while the quotation-free R11 and R32 are dense .969 and .835. Marked mixed honestly: extensive statutory quotation is also what a competent legal comment does, so the parent plausibly touches genuine quality as well.
species.upstream_parent: reliance on an intermediary's prepared material - a watchdog group's talking points, counsel's statutory excerpts - rather than the submitter's own analysis, i.e. a coordination or delegation fingerprint

species.name: Submission-production residue
species.instruction: Score 10 when visible text contains OCR corruption, duplicated headers, raw email routing, attachment placeholders, odd spacing, extraction errors, or other ingest artifacts; score 0 when the prose is cleanly presented.
species.rationale: Production artifacts can become stable model cues while carrying no substantive information. R41 contains severe spacing, OCR, and spelling corruption; R44 contains repeated extraction errors and malformed words; R56 includes raw email metadata and pasted file-processing residue.
species.upstream_parent: document-production, scanning, and docket-ingestion pipeline

species.name: Coordinated copy-paste language
species.instruction: Score 10 when distinctive sentences, paragraph order, statistics, and calls to action are duplicated or nearly duplicated across comments, and 0 when the wording is clearly independently composed.
species.rationale: R35 and R55 are effectively identical, while R28 and R57 repeat the same flavored-cigar template; campaign duplication is predictive of provenance, not independent merit.
species.upstream_parent: Mass advocacy campaign or coordinated comment drive

species.name: Litigation-brief posture
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment adopts an adversarial legal-brief structure with claims of statutory conflict, plain-text mandates, legal jeopardy, formal violations, and requested legal remedies; score 0 when it lacks that posture.
species.rationale: R10 frames the rule as legally jeopardizing miners and argues statutory compulsion, while R39 repeatedly alleges violations of National Standards and demands emergency legal action; counsel involvement may also improve legal substance.
species.upstream_parent: Professional litigation or regulatory-counsel involvement

species.name: Docket-lineage familiarity
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment narrates prior filings, earlier amendments, pilot participation, waivers, agency precedents, or repeated involvement in the same regulatory process; score 0 when it treats the docket as entirely new.
species.rationale: R08 cites earlier AASHTO, coalition, and 2016 submissions; R16 invokes CMS’s prior model practices; and R59 identifies the commenters as original ACAS co-creators after a seven-year pilot.
species.upstream_parent: Existing agency relationship and incumbent participation in the docket

species.name: Agency-native consultation mapping
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment mirrors the notice’s numbered topics or questions, uses agency-specific section labels, limits itself to requested issues, and offers procedural follow-up; score 0 when it is not mapped to the agency’s consultation structure.
species.rationale: R17 answers four FDA information-collection questions explicitly, R36 follows NOAA’s Topic 2 subparagraphs, and R54 answers a numbered FDA hearing question; this process fluency need not equal substantive merit.
species.upstream_parent: Regulatory-affairs sophistication and familiarity with agency consultation procedures

species.name: Deference sandwich
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment opens with thanks or praise, acknowledges the agency’s goals, and then advances a narrowly framed exception or revision; score 0 when it is uniformly supportive, hostile, or uncalibrated.
species.rationale: R03 praises flexibility while raising a focused carcass-marking concern, R06 appreciates Treasury’s effort before isolating one objection, and R25 supports AEB while requesting industry-sensitive implementation; the genre can look thoughtful without proving merit.
species.upstream_parent: Professional lobbying and relationship-preserving drafting norms

species.name: Embodied local witness voice
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment combines a named occupation, residence, family or community identity, and firsthand observations of local effects; score 0 when it contains no personal or locally situated witness account.
species.rationale: R41 identifies an owner-operator and describes customers’ dependence, R45 combines residence with tutoring and hospital experience, and R58 identifies an affected landowner; firsthand experience can be relevant evidence but also acts as a salience cue.
species.upstream_parent: Constituent standing and perceived affectedness of the submitter

species.name: Accusatory moral urgency
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses direct second-person blame, insults, all-caps or emphatic imperatives, catastrophe language, and moral condemnation; score 0 when the register is restrained and technical.
species.rationale: R02 uses insults and a direct command to the FAA, R44 accuses agencies of endangering everyone, and R49 uses repeated all-caps imperatives; emotional arousal is not substantive policy quality.
species.upstream_parent: surface-only

species.name: Attachment-wrapper dependence
species.instruction: Score 10 when the visible submission is mainly a cover note, letterhead, routing information, or “see attached” notice with little substantive text; score 0 when the comment is fully self-contained in the visible text.
species.rationale: R07, R25, R43, R50, and R54 explicitly present formal comments as attached letters, exposing packaging and metadata that may cue the dense model despite the unseen attachment’s contents.
species.upstream_parent: Document-packaging and attachment-submission workflow

species.name: Access-and-continuity choreography
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment signals an ongoing agency relationship through prior meetings, pilot participation, named officials, offers to discuss issues, or collaborative language; score 0 when it is a one-off submission with no such cues.
species.rationale: Relationship-maintenance language can predict perceived consequentiality independently of merit. R11 requests another telephone conference with the agency; R49 calls the commenters original ACAS “co-creators” and emphasizes continued work with CBP and TSA.
species.upstream_parent: existing relationships and privileged access to agency personnel

species.name: Coalition amplification signals
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment speaks for multiple associations or members, endorses allied submissions, names coalition partners, or describes broad sector coverage; score 0 when it presents only an individual, unaffiliated position.
species.rationale: Coalition backing may increase perceived weight without making the particular reasoning stronger. R12 invokes AASHTO and several western-state partners; R49 jointly represents EAA and CAA and identifies their major carrier members.
species.upstream_parent: coordinated mobilization and organizational capacity

species.name: Operational implementation microdetail
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment supplies granular workflow, equipment, filing, validation, staffing, transition, or compliance-process details from inside an affected operation; score 0 when it offers only broad policy preferences or values.
species.rationale: Operational detail can signal an influential insider even when its policy implications are unsupported. R15 discusses PAS validation, platelet yields, licensing, and interstate shipment exceptions; R51 describes reporting systems, controls, unresolved identifiers, and filing-process changes.
species.upstream_parent: submitter proximity to regulated operations and implementation resources

species.name: Campaign provenance artifacts
species.instruction: Score 10 when the text shows coordinated-campaign fingerprints such as duplicated unusual wording, recurring issue order, pasted third-party passages, advocacy-platform metadata, or identical formatting; score 0 when it appears individually authored and bespoke.
species.rationale: Campaign provenance may make a comment appear salient through volume or recognizable advocacy language, not merit. R14 and R18 are nearly identical additive-policy submissions; R21 and R35 repeat the same flavored-cigar text with only location and name changes.
species.upstream_parent: coordinated advocacy campaign or form-letter mobilization

species.name: Authority-borrowing without integration
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment displays statistics, studies, URLs, or agency citations mainly as credibility tokens without explaining methods, uncertainty, or how they establish the requested change; score 0 when it has no such authority display or fully integrates the evidence.
species.rationale: Borrowed authority can inflate perceived sophistication without demonstrating relevance or validity. R05 lists named cobia studies and precise catch figures but gives limited methodological integration; R21 cites market-size and youth-use statistics primarily to support a generic economic narrative.
species.upstream_parent: professional advocacy drafting and credibility signaling

species.name: Personalized grassroots anchoring
species.instruction: Score 10 when a broadly framed policy request is anchored in first-person identity, locality, occupation, personal experience, or a localized emotional hook; score 0 when the submission is impersonal and institutionally framed.
species.rationale: Personalization can signal mobilized public interest without adding reliable evidence about the proposal. R20 and R43 begin with personal health or local-experience hooks before using highly standardized haze language; R57 combines local anecdotes about the Coachella Valley with a general support message.
species.upstream_parent: grassroots constituency activation and personalized form-letter outreach
